newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans corporate governance changes.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans corporate governance changes.

text.p: The Russian government is working on a four-year programme to improve the way companies are run, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Wednesday.

"The government is working on a medium-term plan to reform companies," Yasin told a meeting of American Chamber of Commerce members. "It means they must change their management and asset management practice to make them work more effectively."
The programme, to be adopted by the end of the year, will require companies to clarify management and shareholder rights and duties, giving primacy to shareholder rights, he said.
It will also require Russian companies to introduce international accounting standards and calculate profit tax and value added tax on an accruals rather than cash basis, he said.
Russian accounting standards are designed to plan tax payments rather than provide information about a company's business.
Yasin added the government was planning to help utilities by raising gas, transport and electricity charges for households and replacing subsidised prices by direct poverty benefits.
"This will make it possible to lower the social burden on companies, increase their competitiveness and insure that really poor people receive subsidies, not all and sundry," he said.
